# MLX-Gen Full Documentation Context

> MLX-Gen is a local MLX image and video generation runtime for Apple Silicon. It is published as
> the `mlx-gen` Python package and exposes the `mlxgen` command surface for generation, SeedVR2
> image upscaling, model download, model preparation, capability inspection, and application
> integration.

## Document Index

- `README.md`: project overview, install commands, mflux credit, main workflows, published model links, Wan TI2V/A14B notes, and ecosystem links.
- `docs/README.md`: documentation tree index.
- `docs/getting-started.md`: install, first download, model preparation, image generation, image editing, SeedVR2 image/video restoration and upscaling, and Wan video examples.
- `docs/architecture.md`: system overview and model-file lifecycle diagrams, package shape, command boundaries, runtime failure contract, quantization policy, and the Python integration boundary.
- `docs/api.md`: public CLI, generation routing, public tasks and internal modes, image/video/reference input roles, the `--outpaint-fill`/`--outpaint-fill-color`/`--outpaint-passes` conditioning-canvas options, Bernini R2V/RV2V/V2V options, Wan video controls, SeedVR2 and SwiftVR restoration, runtime events, metadata, and the capability schema (`schema_version` 16, including reference-image bounds, the `restoration` route rows, generated-audio and duration fields, prompt-section descriptors, per-entry defaults, and the outpaint fill and pass contracts).
- `docs/image-edit-modes.md`: plain-language guide to latent img2img, edit-reference, masked edit/inpaint, structured control, multi-reference, generative reframe, and outpaint with its per-side padding and selectable conditioning canvas, including what each mode preserves and what to expect from the output.
- `docs/masked-editing.md`: canonical masked-edit reference — request contract, per-model route matrix with proof grades (Qwen edit/base, Z-Image Turbo, FLUX.2 Klein, video masks; non-turbo Z-Image masked edit is withdrawn for now), per-family behavior including the tunable base-Qwen `--mask-strength` warm start and `effective_steps` metadata, and route selection advice.
- `docs/qwen-route-matrix.md`: current MLX-Gen route truth for Qwen Image and Qwen Image Edit, mapping public `mlxgen` capability ids to the upstream Diffusers Qwen pipeline families and to the proof surfaces that already exist.
- `docs/qwen-localized-editing.md`: plain-language guide to Qwen localized-edit routes, contrasting masked edit/inpaint, structured control, and shipped base-Qwen control-inpaint, defining ControlNet and “sidecar” in user terms, and linking the accepted proof assets.
- `docs/previews.md`: step-wise generation previews rendered with published tiny autoencoders (`taef1` for the FLUX.1 latent space including Z-Image, `taef2` for the FLUX.2 latent space including ERNIE and Bonsai), reproducible tiny-versus-full command pairs with contact sheets, the `--preview-decoder auto|tiny|full` contract, the explicit per-latent-space availability table (mapping is never inferred from latent-channel count), measured fidelity and decode/wall-time costs on M5 Max, the `PreviewDecoder` + `ImageUtil.to_pil_image` application path for realtime preview frames, and the guarantee that final outputs are always full-VAE decoded.
- `docs/upscaling.md`: SeedVR2 image and video restoration guide with official 3B/7B source usage, published 3B/7B q8/q4 package handles, shortest-edge and scale-factor sizing with exact-geometry image restoration (`1x` is pixel-identical to the input), automatic step selection that measures and refines the one-step noise residue on flat/dark content (`--steps` forces a fixed count), the conservative safe-video profile, the `29/8` multi-chunk video floor, accepted five-second Eiffel `1x` and `2x` 3B/7B proof bundles with readable mode labels, reproduction commands, timings/memory data, and real 5x source/output comparisons.
- `docs/edit-capabilities.md`: image-edit and adjacent structured-control contact sheets, model/package status summaries, the published outpaint capability fields including `outpaint_preservation` and the per-route validated envelope, the cross-route outpaint matrix and the axis-coverage bundle, and exact command logs for Qwen Image Edit, Qwen Image Edit 2509/2511, base Qwen structured control, FLUX.2 Klein, latent I2I rows, and the masked-edit 5x5 matrix grading the FLUX.2 Klein, base-Qwen native, and Z-Image non-turbo masked routes. FIBO Edit is unsupported through unified `mlxgen generate`.
- `docs/reframe-outpaint.md`: reframe/outpaint workflows, per-side padding and how to extend one side, one axis, or all four in a single call, the `--outpaint-fill` conditioning-canvas modes and how `auto` resolves them, padding guidance including the automatic two-pass split of deep two-axis requests (`--outpaint-passes`), the measured corner-depth sweep and its remedies, exact commands, strict FLUX.2 Klein outpaint on distilled 4B/9B (guidance 1.0) and base 4B/9B (guidance 4.0), the cross-route outpaint matrix running every supported route on one source with per-route timings and source drift, the 2026-09-02 axis-coverage sheets across three source aspect ratios and eight padding configurations, and the three related validation profile ids.
- `docs/lora.md`: route-specific LoRA capability fields, explicit adapter download, strict scale matching, exact adapter/base-model compatibility, source/no-LoRA/with-LoRA validation, exact public proof rows for current Qwen, Z-Image, FLUX.2, ERNIE, and Wan routes, including base Qwen latent, the exact `AbstractFramework/z-image-turbo-8bit` latent children's-drawing row, Qwen 2511 multi-reference/reframe/outpaint, FLUX.2 Klein 9B multi-reference, FLUX.2 Klein base 4B outpaint, direct `lightx2v/Wan2.2-Lightning` download, MiniMax-H3 adapters in both the diffusers and the original-checkpoint key layouts stacked on the Turbo adapter, and explicit guidance that the validated Lightning target is the MLX-Gen q8 package rather than an arbitrary external FP8 checkpoint.
- `docs/wan-video.md`: practical Wan2.2 T2V/I2V guidance, plain and masked prompt-guided A14B video-to-video with the exact reproducible proof commands and included artifacts, output canvas and source mapping (`--canvas-policy`, `--resize-mode`), repeat-run and application performance options (prompt-embed disk cache, resident text encoder, health-check opt-out, opt-in compiled transformer, A14B inactive-expert release), broader A14B target size families, and `101`-frame, 20 fps M5 Max comparison clips for A14B and TI2V-5B.
- `docs/minimax-h3.md`: MiniMax-H3 text-to-video and first-frame image-to-video (`--image-path`) with a synchronized stereo AAC soundtrack in one MP4: `minimax-h3`, `minimax-h3-turbo`, `minimax-h3-turbo-544p`, lightx2v Turbo adapters, the structured prompt sections, frame and canvas rules, `--quantize 8` load-time quantization, measured M5 Max runtime and memory, the `audio_*` metadata contract, Python usage, verification summary, and current limits, and community LoRA adapters in the original-checkpoint key layout stacked on the Turbo adapter with `--lora-paths`, with the included with/without evidence clips.
- `docs/bernini.md`: experimental Bernini-R 1.3B reference-to-video and video-edit routes, pinned BF16 runtime setup and download sizes, the committed official public parity bundle with full prompts and contact sheets per upstream example row, and task-specific recipes for many-reference binding and structure-changing edits.
- `docs/recommendations.md`: conservative model recommendations for `18 GB`, `24 GB`, `32 GB`, `64 GB`, and `128+ GB` Macs based on published MLX-Gen memory measurements.
- `docs/examples/spaceship-snow.md`: complete model-backed workflow across T2I, I2I edit, multi-reference I2I, T2V A14B, and I2V A14B.
- `docs/model-management.md`: explicit `download` and `prepare`, local packages, factored Bernini setup and disk preflight, matching Hugging Face handle resolution, and `DownloadRequiredError`.
- `docs/quantization.md`: published package matrix, model-specific q8/q4/BF16 policies, Wan storage/runtime behavior, Bernini's BF16-only gate, and Bonsai ternary support.
- `docs/huggingface-publishing.md`: generated model cards and AbstractFramework Hugging Face upload guidance.
- `docs/python-integration.md`: embedding MLX-Gen, route-resolved runtime loading, `model_kwargs` constructor passthrough (resident text encoder, prompt-cache opt-out), runtime memory defaults for hosts (`MFLUX_MLX_CACHE_LIMIT_GB`, `-1` unlimited opt-out, host-managed `mx.set_cache_limit` detection, `MFLUX_NO_WEIGHT_PREFETCH`), Wan `last_image_path`, `context_image_paths`/`context_noise`, and `denoising_step_list` generation kwargs, `save_kwargs` including `validate_health=False`, serial multi-output reuse for unified `mlxgen generate` families, overwrite/collision behavior, the outpaint/reframe pipeline (`run_outpaint`, `prepare_outpaint`, `prepare_reframe`, and the `post_process` before-save hook on `generate_outputs`), SeedVR2's direct-model boundary, progress callbacks, AbstractVision/AbstractCore integration, and threading behavior.
- `docs/faq.md`: common conceptual questions, I2I mode selection and output sizing, SeedVR2 image/video sizing and default audio-preservation behavior, Qwen edit variants, negative prompts, reframe/outpaint, Wan resolutions, long image-to-video shot guidance (81-frame budget and continuation routes), prompting guidance, usage limits, and why MLX-Gen q8 Lightning guidance should not be generalized to arbitrary FP8 checkpoints.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: user-facing failure symptoms, diagnostics, fixes including how to choose the outpaint conditioning canvas when the padded area continues the border texture, and legacy `mflux-generate-*` migration guidance.
- `docs/release.md`: release and publishing process.

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: local development and pull-request expectations.
- `SECURITY.md`: vulnerability reporting and safety guidance.

---

## Project Summary

MLX-Gen runs supported image and video generation models locally with MLX. It started as a fork of
`filipstrand/mflux`, and most credit for the current codebase remains with Filip Strand and the
original mflux contributors. MLX-Gen now publishes independently as `mlx-gen` and exposes `mlxgen`
as the public command surface. It keeps the mflux foundation and focuses on predictable local
generation for real applications: users download or prepare models before running a job, then use
one command to generate, inspect supported modes, and compare generated examples and measured
results. MLX-Gen contributes by adding tested T2I/I2I routes, Qwen Image Edit 2509/2511 routing
and parity fixes, Bonsai Image support, Wan2.2 text-to-video, image-to-video, and prompt-guided
video-to-video support, Bernini-R reference video generation/editing, model-specific quantization
policies, published MLX-Gen optimized
packages, and progress callbacks for apps. The fork exists so AbstractFramework projects can move
quickly without losing the option to
merge useful changes back upstream if that becomes valuable for the wider mflux community.

The project focuses on practical Apple Silicon workflows:

- generation from local model files after explicit setup;
- local MLX-Gen model packages, including quantized layouts;
- Qwen Image/Edit, FLUX.2 Klein, Z-Image, ERNIE Image Turbo, Bonsai Image, base FIBO, Wan2.2, Bernini-R, and SeedVR2 support;
- model capability inspection before heavy runs;
- progress events and live preview frames for applications;
- integration with AbstractVision, AbstractCore, AbstractFramework, and AbstractFlow.

Some implementation internals still use the original `mflux.*` package layout. New user-facing
commands and integrations should prefer `mlxgen`.

---

## Runtime Contract

MLX-Gen separates setup from generation:

- `mlxgen download` explicitly downloads model artifacts into the local cache.
- `mlxgen prepare` explicitly creates reusable local MLX-Gen model packages and generated model cards.
- `mlxgen generate` runs from downloaded source files or local MLX-Gen packages and does not start network downloads.
- `mlxgen capabilities` inspects route-supported public tasks, internal modes, and option support without loading weights.
- `mlxgen validation` reports generated-output and benchmark records for exact model/package rows; it is separate from route support.

Missing model, tokenizer, LoRA, or Depth Pro artifacts raise `DownloadRequiredError` with explicit
download or prepare commands. This behavior is important for application integrations because long
jobs should not unexpectedly start a network transfer.

CLI multi-output is seed-driven: `--seed` accepts multiple explicit seeds, `--auto-seeds` is
available on `mlxgen generate` and `mlxgen upscale`, duplicate explicit seeds are rejected,
underlying model methods remain singular, and unified `mlxgen generate` Python families also
expose `load_generation_model(...).generate_outputs(...)` for serial multi-output reuse. SeedVR2
upscale remains on direct `SeedVR2` methods rather than that wrapper.

A complete local MLX-Gen package under `./models/<repo-name>` can satisfy a matching Hugging Face handle.
For example, `./models/wan2.2-i2v-a14b-diffusers-8bit` can be used when generation is requested as
`AbstractFramework/wan2.2-i2v-a14b-diffusers-8bit`, as long as the folder contains all required
indexes and shard files.

---

## Public Tasks And Internal Modes

Public tasks describe media direction:

- `text-to-image`
- `image-to-image`
- `text-to-video`
- `image-to-video`
- `video-to-video`

Image editing is not a separate public task. It is an internal image-to-image mode. The resolver
uses model capabilities, image count, and options to choose a generation plan:

- no image: text-to-image or text-to-video when the model supports it;
- one image and video model: image-to-video;
- one image plus `--image-strength`: latent img2img;
- one image with FLUX.2 or a dedicated edit checkpoint and no `--image-strength`: edit/reference I2I;
- one image with a latent image model such as ERNIE Image Turbo, Z-Image, or base Qwen Image: latent img2img only when `--image-strength` is explicit;
- repeated `--image`: multi-reference I2I when supported;
- repeatable `--reference-image`: a separate semantic conditioning role for VACE and Bernini;
- one to eight Bernini references without a primary image: reference-to-video under the public
  `text-to-video` task; one source video plus references: reference-guided `video-to-video`;
- mask/fill options: accepted only by mask/fill capabilities; canvas outpaint options are accepted
  only by capabilities that advertise `supports_outpaint=true`.

Applications can use `get_model_capabilities(...)` and `resolve_generation_plan(...)` from the
`mlxgen` package to make the same routing decision before launching a job. Applications can use
`get_model_validation(...)` when they need current release-evidence status for an exact
model/package.

Ordinary image-to-image defaults to `source-aspect` canvas resolution. The first input image is the
geometry anchor for latent img2img, edit/reference I2I, and multi-reference I2I. `--width` and
`--height` are size targets; use `--canvas-policy exact-resize` only when the exact requested
canvas is intentional. `--resize-mode` is orthogonal: the policy picks the output canvas, the mode
picks how source pixels map onto it - `resize` stretches to fill (default), `crop` center-crops
without distortion, `pad` letterboxes the full source without distortion. Masks always map through
the same source-to-canvas geometry as the pixels, and letterboxed borders count as preserved
regions. Latent image-to-image routes (Qwen, FLUX.2 Klein, Z-Image, ERNIE, FIBO, FLUX.1), Qwen
native masked edit, Z-Image native inpaint, and the Wan video routes accept the flag;
reference-pinned routes (edit/reference, controlnet, outpaint/reframe) reject it loudly.
`mlxgen capabilities` advertises per-route `resize_modes` (and `canvas_policies` on Wan video
rows). Generated image metadata records the canvas policy, resize mode, requested size, source
image size, and final output size, and both values replay via `--config-from-metadata`.

`--image-strength` belongs only to latent img2img. Edit/reference and multi-reference I2I use
source images as conditioning or references, so MLX-Gen rejects `--image-strength` for those modes
before loading weights. Generative reframe is available through `--reframe-padding`
for models that advertise `supports_reframe=true`; it asks the edit model to generate a larger view
and may redraw source content. Outpaint is available through `--outpaint-padding` for
capabilities that advertise `supports_outpaint=true`, and each route publishes its source-region
guarantee as `outpaint_preservation`, and every route publishes the same one,
`adaptive-content-aware-source-blend`: the source region is held in latent space behind a narrow
transition band while the added area is denoised (Qwen Image Edit through its masked-edit input,
FLUX.2 Klein through its own lock), then the original crop is pasted back while the generated
source window still matches it. FLUX.2 Klein runs it on every Klein model: distilled 4B/9B publish
`flux2.outpaint` alongside `flux2.reframe` and run at guidance 1.0, and base 4B/9B publish
`flux2.outpaint` only and run at guidance 4.0. Omit
`--guidance` and each model takes its own default; passing a value above 1.0 to distilled Klein is
rejected before the weights load. Outpaint padding takes CSS-style `top,right,bottom,left` values
and each side is independent, so one call can extend a single side, both sides of an axis, or all
four at different depths; `0` leaves that edge where it is. Published proof covers
`black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-base-4B` and `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-base-9B` as source
models, `AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-base-4b-8bit` as the exact base prepared-package row, and
`AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-4b-8bit` and `AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-9b-8bit` as the exact
distilled prepared-package rows. Unsupported model families reject
`--outpaint-padding` before loading weights. `--outpaint-padding` computes `--width` and `--height`
from the source and the padding and runs at `exact-resize`, so it rejects `--width`, `--height`,
and `--canvas-policy`, and cannot be combined with `--reframe-padding` or `--mask-path`.

The unified CLI accepts both `--negative-prompt` and `--negative`. Python callers pass the same
value as `negative_prompt=...` on the model-specific generation method. For Qwen image edit,
guidance above `1` uses true classifier-free guidance when a negative prompt is present; MLX-Gen
uses the official blank negative-prompt behavior for Qwen edit models when the option is omitted.
FLUX.2 Klein base models (`flux2-klein-base-4b`, `flux2-klein-base-9b` and their prepared
packages) accept a negative prompt on every route and run classifier-free guidance against it; it
needs `--guidance` above 1.0, and omitting `--guidance` with a negative prompt selects the base
default of 4.0. Distilled Klein weights have no guidance branch, so `mlxgen generate` rejects
`--negative-prompt` for them before loading weights. Every capability row publishes
`supports_negative_prompt` (`false` on distilled FLUX.2 Klein and Bonsai rows).

## Outpaint Conditioning Canvas

Outpaint pastes the source onto a larger canvas and asks the model to complete the added area, so
what fills that area before denoising decides much of the result. Routes that advertise
`supports_outpaint_fill=true` - the FLUX.2 Klein outpaint route - accept `--outpaint-fill`
with `auto` (default), `edge`, `neutral`, `solid`, or `blur`:

- `edge` stretches the source border strip outward, continuing an existing texture across the
  padding. Past the depth that strip covers - the edge-fill reach - it reads as directional streaks.
- `neutral` paints a flat per-side border color sampled from the source. There is nothing to
  continue, so the model generates new subject matter, and there is no hard color step at the seam.
- `solid` paints one flat color, taken from `--outpaint-fill-color` (`R,G,B` with 0-255 per channel,
  or `#rrggbb`). Without that option, `solid` uses `0,255,0` when a green-border outpaint adapter is
  loaded and the source's mean border color otherwise.
- `blur` paints a blurred, scaled copy of the source, for a soft background suggestion.
- `auto` keeps `edge` while every padded side stays within the edge-fill reach, switches to
  `neutral` past that, and switches to `solid` green when a green-border outpaint adapter is loaded,
  because those adapters are trained to paint into a pure-green canvas.

`--outpaint-fill-color` applies only to `solid`; `edge`, `neutral`, and `blur` derive their canvas
from the source. Both options require `--outpaint-padding`, are recorded in generation metadata, and
replay through `--config-from-metadata`. The Qwen edit backend takes no fill option and always
builds an edge-extended canvas.

Every outpaint run prints its resolved canvas to stderr before denoising, and names the reason when
`auto` chose the mode:

```text
Outpaint: fill=neutral, canvas 928x1536 from source 768x766, padding top=0 right=76 bottom=766 left=76.
Outpaint: --outpaint-fill auto selected neutral because the deepest padding is bottom 766px (100% of
the source height), 2.0x the 384px edge-fill reach; the fill conditions the seam around the source
rather than the padded region, and a blank seam does not hand the model a stretched border strip to
continue.
```

A request that pads a vertical side and a horizontal side deeply opens a free corner that shares
neither a row nor a column with the source, and the failure mode there is subject duplication, a
second copy of the subject painted into that corner (measured on distilled 9B: clean up to 30% on
both axes, duplicating on two to three seeds at 50-60%). `--outpaint-passes` decides how such a
request runs: `auto` (default) splits it into two single-axis passes - the deeper axis first on the
source, the other axis on that output - when the shallower axis depth exceeds the route's published
`outpaint_auto_split_corner_ratio` (0.3 on every current route); `2` splits any two-axis request;
`1` forces one canvas and prints a warning naming the corner. The split reaches exactly the one-pass
canvas, is clean on three of three seeds where one pass duplicated on three of three, costs a
second denoise, and on the latent-locked FLUX.2 routes roughly doubles the recorded source drift
(about 8-10 against 4-5 on distilled 9B) because the source goes through the lock and the VAE
twice; Qwen restores the original pixels after the last pass. Prompt content is the other lever:
describe the area being added rather than the subject, which the source already conditions the
model on. Raising `--steps` does not move duplication (measured at 16, 32 and 48 steps). On the
latent-locked FLUX.2 Klein routes `--outpaint-fill` is not a lever over it either, because the
fill conditions the seam around the source and never the free corner. Every run prints its pass
plan to stderr, and metadata records `outpaint_passes`, `outpaint_passes_requested`,
`outpaint_pass_paddings`, `outpaint_pass_fills`, `outpaint_pass_reason`, and per pass
`outpaint_pass_source_restore_differences` / `outpaint_pass_source_restore_applied`; the resolved
count replays through `--config-from-metadata`. Each pass applies the route's preservation against
its own source before the original is measured and restored, so Qwen's original pixels come through
a split run exactly as through a single one.

Applications can read the same contract as JSON without running a job. Outpaint-capable capability
rows carry `supports_outpaint_fill`, `outpaint_fill_modes`, `outpaint_default_fill_mode`,
`outpaint_auto_edge_fill_max_stretch`, `outpaint_recommended_lora`, `outpaint_preservation`,
`outpaint_validated_padding`, `outpaint_validated_fill_mode`,
`outpaint_validated_max_canvas_pixels`, `outpaint_pass_modes` (`["auto", "1", "2"]`),
`outpaint_default_passes` (`"auto"`), and `outpaint_auto_split_corner_ratio` (`0.3`, or `null` on
a route that never splits). On
`AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-base-4b-8bit`, `flux2.outpaint` reports
`supports_outpaint_fill: true`, `outpaint_fill_modes: ["auto", "edge", "neutral", "solid", "blur"]`,
`outpaint_default_fill_mode: "auto"`, `outpaint_auto_edge_fill_max_stretch: 12.0`,
`outpaint_recommended_lora: "fal/flux-2-klein-4B-outpaint-lora"`, and
`outpaint_preservation: "adaptive-content-aware-source-blend"`. On
`AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-4b-8bit` and `AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-9b-8bit`,
`flux2.outpaint` reports the same contract with `outpaint_recommended_lora: null`, because the
green-canvas adapter's A/B proof is a base row. On
`AbstractFramework/qwen-image-edit-2511-8bit`, `qwen.outpaint` reports
`supports_outpaint_fill: false`, `outpaint_fill_modes: ["edge"]`,
`outpaint_default_fill_mode: "edge"`, and
`outpaint_preservation: "adaptive-content-aware-source-blend"`. `outpaint_recommended_lora` and the
`outpaint_validated_*` envelope are published per route, so a row states only its own evidence;
these rows happen to share one envelope, `"5%,80%,5%,60%"` padding with `edge` fill and `282880`
maximum canvas pixels. Outside that envelope outpaint is supported but unvalidated.
`outpaint_recommended_lora` is optional; the route runs without it. A route publishing
`supports_outpaint_fill: false` accepts only the mode named by
`outpaint_default_fill_mode`; `mlxgen generate` refuses any other before dispatch, naming the
capability and the fixed canvas. Generated metadata records `outpaint_fill`, `outpaint_fill_color`,
`outpaint_fill_requested`, `outpaint_fill_reason`, `outpaint_edge_fill_reach_px`,
`outpaint_edge_fill_overreach`, `outpaint_preservation`, and
`outpaint_source_restore_difference`.

Python hosts run the same pipeline through `mlxgen.run_outpaint(loaded=..., source_image=...,
padding=..., seeds=[...], prompt=...)`, or build the canvas without loading weights through
`mlxgen.prepare_outpaint(...)` / `mlxgen.prepare_reframe(...)` and call `session.generate(model,
...)`. `LoadedGenerationModel.generate_outputs(..., post_process=<callable>)` is the hook that runs
on each artifact after generation and before save.

Two limits are worth planning around. First, the paste back is conditional on the generated source
window staying within the restore threshold (24 mean-abs), which the latent lock keeps it inside
on every recorded run, and the transition band along the seam is regenerated. Every run records
`outpaint_source_restore_difference`: the mean absolute difference (0-255) between the source crop
and the model's own output in that region, measured before the restore, and
`outpaint_source_restore_applied`. Use masked editing
(`--mask-path`) when a region must stay untouched. Second, outpaint cost scales with the expanded
canvas and attention cost grows faster than canvas area, so extending in two moderate passes is
cheaper and generally better than one large pass.

Measured on one 432x240 starship crop at padding `5%,80%,5%,60%` (a 1040x272 canvas, `auto`
resolving to `edge`) on an Apple M5 Max, 40-core GPU, 128 GB unified memory: distilled Klein 4B q8
54.6 s at source drift 6.01, distilled Klein 9B q8 80.6 s at 3.72, base Klein 4B q8 72.2 s at 5.61,
base Klein 9B q8 100.0 s at 4.03, and Qwen Image Edit 2511 q8 341.1 s at 9.35. Time is the whole
command including weight load. Distilled Klein 4B is the fastest route, the 9B models hold the
source closest, and Qwen is the only route in the set that accepts a negative prompt. Full table and
command log: `docs/reframe-outpaint.md` and
`docs/assets/validation/outpaint-model-matrix-2026-09-01/`.

Per-side coverage is published separately, on `AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-9b-8bit` at 16 steps,
guidance 1, seed 99 and an empty prompt: three source aspect ratios (landscape 640x448, square
512x512, portrait 448x640) each run through eight padding configurations - every single side, both
vertical sides, both horizontal sides, all four sides, and an asymmetric four-side request. Contact
sheets, per-band measurements against the conditioning canvas, and the command log are in
`docs/assets/validation/outpaint-axis-coverage-2026-09-02/`, described in
`docs/reframe-outpaint.md` under "Expanding On Any Side".

## Choosing Image Edit Modes

MLX-Gen exposes one public `image-to-image` task, but models can support different edit behaviors:

- `latent-img2img`: whole-image variation or restyle from one source image. Use it for mood,
  lighting, or style changes across the whole frame. `--image-strength` controls how far the output
  may drift.
- `edit-reference`: instruction editing from one source image. Use it when you want better
  composition hold while changing appearance, object state, or scene treatment.
- `multi-reference`: composition from several reference images. The first image is the geometry
  anchor and later images provide additional style, material, or lighting cues.
- masked edit / inpaint: localized edit through `--image` plus `--mask-path` on routes that
  advertise `supports_mask=true`. White mask pixels are repainted and black pixels are preserved.
  Mask-capable rows: Qwen edit models (`qwen.inpaint`), base Qwen models (`qwen.base-inpaint`
  natively with a tunable `--mask-strength` warm start - default 0.85 anchors structure, 0.95
  repaints fully with per-seed color fidelity - plus `mask_strength`/`effective_steps` metadata,
  or `qwen.control-inpaint`
  with the auto-injected InstantX sidecar on the exact `AbstractFramework/qwen-image-8bit`
  row), Z-Image Turbo (`z-image.inpaint`; non-turbo masked requests are rejected for the
  moment after measured geometry failures), and FLUX.2 Klein distilled and base models
  (`flux2.inpaint`, a diffusers `Flux2KleinInpaintPipeline` port with per-step source
  compositing; the backend `mflux-generate-flux2-edit` command additionally accepts extra
  images after the source as masked-area references). `--image-strength` is rejected together
  with `--mask-path`. `docs/masked-editing.md` is the canonical matrix and behavior page.
- `generative reframe`: zoom-out style edit through `--reframe-padding`. It generates a larger
  scene and may redraw subject details inside the original crop.
- `outpaint`: canvas extension through `--outpaint-padding`, independent per side, starting from a
  conditioning canvas that `--outpaint-fill` selects on FLUX.2 Klein routes. It aims to keep the
  source region more stable than reframe, but it is still generative rather than a literal
  pixel-lock guarantee.

Use `mlxgen capabilities --model <model>` to check whether the selected model supports the mode you
want. Use [docs/image-edit-modes.md](docs/image-edit-modes.md) for examples and
[docs/edit-capabilities.md](docs/edit-capabilities.md) for exact model/package proof assets.

LoRA support is route-specific. LoRA adapters are required inputs, not optional
hints. Generation does not download LoRAs. Use
`mlxgen download --model <adapter-repo> --all-files`, then pass a local `.safetensors` path or
`owner/repo:filename.safetensors`. `mlxgen capabilities` reports `supports_lora`, `lora_status`,
`lora_target_roles`, and `lora_validation_profile` per route. `mapped-unvalidated` means a mapping
exists but the exact model/package has not yet passed a visible accepted-adapter A/B validation.
`--lora-scales` must have exactly one value per adapter. MLX-Gen rejects known incompatible
adapter/base-model pairs when cached model-card metadata is available and also checks LoRA matrix
shapes during application. For example, `lovis93/Flux-2-Multi-Angles-LoRA-v2` targets
`black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev`, while current FLUX.2 support is Klein 4B/9B, so that adapter is not
accepted for Klein routes. Validate LoRA effects with the same source, prompt, dimensions, seed,
steps, and guidance with and without the adapter. Current exact proof rows include original Qwen
Image Edit q8, Qwen Image Edit 2509 q8, Qwen Image Edit 2511 q8, base Qwen Image q8 text and
latent, Qwen Image 2512 q8 text, Z-Image Turbo q8 text and latent, FLUX.2 Klein 9B q8 edit and
multi-reference, FLUX.2 Klein base 4B q8 outpaint, ERNIE Image Turbo q8 text and latent, and the
current Wan q8 public video rows. Bonsai remains fail-closed
because its packed runtime does not expose the standard replaceable linear-module boundary the
current LoRA loader requires.

The Qwen edit checkpoints are distinct. `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit` is single-reference edit only
(`max_images=1`). `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509` and `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` expose
multi-reference edit routes when the selected package supports and validates that
route.

`docs/edit-capabilities.md` is the current visual evidence page for image editing. It publishes the
regular Qwen Image Edit base/q8/q4 contact sheet, the Qwen Image Edit 2511 source/q8/q4 parity
sheet, the 5x4 distilled FLUX.2/Qwen Image Edit 2509 matrices, the 2026-06-08 reframe/outpaint
source/q8/q4 matrices, the 2026-06-10 FLUX.2 Klein base source-model starship
matrix and seam review, the 2026-09-01 FLUX.2 Klein latent-locked outpaint rows, the 2026-09-01
cross-route outpaint model matrix, and links the
exact command logs used for the validation profiles. In the
documented spaceship profiles, distilled FLUX.2 Klein 4B/9B q4/q8 pass latent, edit-reference,
multi-reference, and generative reframe rows; their q8 packages pass strict outpaint on the
2026-09-01 latent-lock profile, and their 2026-06-08 outpaint artifacts are retained as historical
evidence for the edit path with adaptive source blending;
FLUX.2 Klein base 9B source passes latent, edit-reference, multi-reference, and strict outpaint on
the starship case; FLUX.2 Klein base 4B source passes latent, edit-reference, and strict outpaint
with a partial multi-reference row; Qwen Image Edit 2509 source/q8 pass the edit-reference and
multi-reference rows while q4 is partial on composition; Qwen Image Edit, 2509, and 2511
source/q8/q4 pass the 2026-06-08 reframe/outpaint profile. Qwen Image Edit 2511 source/q8/q4 pass the
2026-06-06 pencil sketch, hard-landing edit, and multi-reference composition profile. FIBO Edit is
unsupported through unified `mlxgen generate` in the current release.

---

## Restoration And Upscaling

`mlxgen upscale` hosts two promptless restoration families, selected with `--model`. Neither is
routed through `mlxgen generate`.

- SeedVR2 (`seedvr2`, `seedvr2-3b`, `seedvr2-7b`, `seedvr2-7b-sharp`, official ByteDance repos,
  AbstractFramework packages) restores images and video and can scale. Quantized q8/q4 packages
  exist.
- SwiftVR (`swiftvr`, `swiftvr-5b`) restores video in one step at the source resolution on a
  Wan2.2-TI2V-5B backbone. It does not restore stills, does not scale, and runs bf16 only. Clip
  length must satisfy `frames % 4 == 1`; the CLI trims and reports the trim. Measured on an M4 Max
  over 121 frames at 384x288, SwiftVR restored in 11.5 s against 471.0 s for SeedVR2-3B and 458.8 s
  for SeedVR2-7B, at 11.1 GB peak MLX against 57.9 GB and 67.8 GB. SwiftVR reinterprets texture
  where SeedVR2 recovers it, so it is the throughput route rather than the fidelity route, and it is
  an offline batch route on Apple Silicon rather than a real-time one (1080p measures about
  1.1 FPS).

Both families are described by the `restoration` array of `mlxgen capabilities`, which reports
`accepted_media`, `max_images`/`max_videos`, `supports_scaling` and `scale_factors`,
`supports_quantization` and `weight_precision`, the `frame_multiple`/`frame_remainder` clip
contract, and the temporal chunking contract. `max_images: 0` is how a family states that it cannot
restore stills, so a caller never has to match handle strings.

In Python, both families expose `restore_video_to_path(...)` with an identical keyword-only core,
and SeedVR2 additionally exposes `restore_image_to_path(...)` alongside the in-memory
`generate_image(...)`. A caller selects a route by input kind rather than by model family.

`--resolution` accepts either an integer shorter-edge target or a scale factor:

- `--resolution 1024` sets the shorter output edge to 1024px and preserves source aspect ratio.
- `--resolution 2x` doubles both source dimensions.
- `--resolution 3x` triples both source dimensions.

For a `320x192` source, `2x` resolves to `640x384` and `3x` resolves to `960x576`. Integer
shortest-edge sizing is useful for predictable target classes across mixed source ratios; scale
factors are useful for direct 2x/3x comparisons. SeedVR2 also restores and denoises, so near-source
target sizes mainly validate restoration behavior rather than visible super-resolution quality.
Image restoration preserves the requested geometry exactly: `1x` returns the input dimensions
pixel-for-pixel with no resampling (divisibility is satisfied with reflective padding cropped
away after decode), and integer targets keep the exact source aspect ratio. Video restoration
center-crops frames to multiples of 16, matching the official pipeline. On flat or dark content
(night scenes, astrophotography), the official one-step image inference can retain residual
sampling noise that decodes as a faint 8-pixel mesh texture; the default steps mode is
automatic — the single official step, plus a measured 4-step refinement only when that artifact
is actually detected in the output (recorded in metadata as `steps_mode` and
`one_step_residue_pct`). `--steps 1`-`4` forces a fixed count on image inputs.

Use `--softness 0.25` to `0.5` when noisy source texture should be smoothed before reconstruction.
`--softness 0.0` keeps source conditioning most direct; higher values can suppress grain or JPEG
texture but can soften fine detail. SeedVR2 keeps small image outputs untiled, automatically uses
tiled VAE decode for large image outputs, and uses tiled encode/decode when `--vae-tiling` is set
for image runs. Video restore rejects `--vae-tiling`; the public safe video profile defaults to
`1x`, enables `--low-ram` automatically, uses sequential temporal chunking, and rejects enlarged
video output unless `--force-unsafe-video-memory` is passed explicitly. Multi-chunk SeedVR2 video
profiles below `29` source frames and `8` overlap frames are rejected to protect temporal
continuity.

`docs/upscaling.md` includes published `AbstractFramework/seedvr2-3b-8bit`,
`AbstractFramework/seedvr2-3b-4bit`, `AbstractFramework/seedvr2-7b-8bit`, and
`AbstractFramework/seedvr2-7b-4bit` usage, plus checked-in 5x comparisons: a `133x113` source
enlarged to the generated `658x560` size next to SeedVR2 3B and 7B source/q8/q4 outputs generated
with `--resolution 5x`, `--seed 42`, and `--metadata`. It also includes the accepted June 21
five-second Eiffel archival proof bundles for the accepted `1x` and `2x` 3B/7B video route,
including comparison MP4s, motion strips, readable validation reports, timings, memory notes, and
reproduction commands.

---

## Reproducible Example

`docs/examples/spaceship-snow.md` is the primary complete example. It downloads:

- `AbstractFramework/flux.2-klein-9b-8bit`
- `AbstractFramework/wan2.2-t2v-a14b-diffusers-8bit`
- `AbstractFramework/wan2.2-i2v-a14b-diffusers-8bit`

It then generates:

- a text-to-image spaceship in snow;
- a single-image pencil-sketch edit;
- a single-image crash-in-snow edit;
- a multi-reference image composition using the sketch style and crash layout;
- a Wan A14B text-to-video takeoff clip;
- a Wan A14B image-to-video takeoff clip from the generated source image.

The included docs assets contain the generated images, video frame strips, MP4 files, and a contact
sheet assembled from real outputs.

---

## Wan Video Sizes

Wan frame counts are normalized to `4n + 1`, and duration is `frames / fps`. Width and height are
normalized up to the selected model's VAE/patch multiple:

- TI2V-5B T2V/I2V requires 32-pixel multiples. Recommended/native quality sizes are `1280x704` and
  `704x1280`; practical lower-cost sizes include `832x480`, `480x832`, `448x256`, and `256x448`.
  `1280x720` adjusts to `1280x736`, and `432x240` adjusts to `448x256`.
- T2V-A14B and I2V-A14B require 16-pixel multiples. Recommended/native quality sizes are
  `1280x720` and `720x1280`; practical lower-cost sizes include `832x480`, `480x832`, `448x256`,
  `256x448`, and `432x240`.

Lower-cost sizes are useful for routing checks and prompt iteration. For practical five-second
clips on an M5 Max, A14B at `480x240` or `240x480`, `101` frames, 20 fps, and `20-25` steps has
produced good local results in about 30 minutes for the documented starship profile. TI2V-5B at
`832x480`, `101` frames, 20 fps, and 25 steps took about 12 minutes but was weaker visually;
TI2V-5B at `1280x704` took about 35 minutes and improved without matching the A14B result. Use
recommended/native size, frame count, and step count when judging upstream-scale model quality.

For Wan image-to-video, `width` and `height` are size targets by default. MLX-Gen resolves the
final output canvas from the source image aspect ratio and the selected model's spatial multiple
before conditioning the model, so portrait sources remain portrait and landscape sources remain
landscape. The video is generated directly at that resolved canvas; it is not generated at a
stretched canvas and then cropped or resized afterward. Pass `--canvas-policy exact-resize` to
honor the requested (multiple-adjusted) canvas instead, with `--resize-mode` (`resize` stretch,
`crop`, or `pad` letterbox) choosing how the source maps onto it. With `--json-events`, the
`start` runtime event carries the resolved output `width`/`height`. Typical resolved outputs
include:

- I2V-A14B with a `16:9` source and `1280x720` target: `1280x720`.
- I2V-A14B with a `9:16` source and `1280x720` target: `720x1280`.
- I2V-A14B with a `1:1` source and `432x240` target: `320x320`.
- TI2V-5B I2V with a `20:11` source and `1280x704` target: `1280x704`.
- TI2V-5B I2V with a `16:9` source and `1280x704` target: `1248x704`.
- TI2V-5B I2V with a `1:1` source and `432x240` target: `320x320`.

Saved metadata records requested dimensions, source image dimensions, and resolved output
dimensions. To get an exact I2V output size, prepare the source at the same aspect ratio as the
target and choose dimensions that match the model multiple.

Wan A14B image-to-video can additionally pin the END of the clip to a second anchor image with
`--last-image <path>` (Python: `last_image_path=...`), the diffusers `last_image` first+last
bracket conditioning. The last image maps through the same resolved canvas and `--resize-mode`
as the first frame, so match their aspect ratios. It requires `--image-path` and is rejected on
TI2V-5B (`expand_timesteps`), Wan VACE, and text/video-to-video. The path is recorded in
metadata (`last_image_path`), replayed by `--config-from-metadata`, and advertised as the
additive `supports_last_image` field on the `wan.first-frame` capability row. Official
first+last training exists for Wan 2.1 (FLF2V); on Wan 2.2 A14B
this ships as EXPERIMENTAL: the shipped probe measured end-frame adherence at MAE 4.6/255 vs
the target (first-frame-only baseline: 56.1) with no mid-clip exposure jumps on one Lightning
4-step storyboard pair whose target was a real future frame of the same shot — treat broader
recipes (other step counts, out-of-distribution targets) as unverified.

Wan A14B image-to-video can also CONTINUE an existing shot with real momentum:
`--context-frames <png>...` (Python: `context_image_paths=[...]`) extends the conditioned head
with the ordered frames that FOLLOW `--image-path` in the motion being continued (the
SkyReels-V2/SVI-class multi-frame handover). The head `[image, *context]` must fill whole 4x
VAE latent groups — 4, 8, or 12 context frames = heads 5, 9, 13 — and needs
`--frames >= head + 4`; it composes with `--last-image`, maps every frame through the first
frame's canvas and `--resize-mode`, and is rejected on TI2V-5B (`expand_timesteps`), Wan VACE,
and text/video-to-video before the weight load. `--context-noise <0-1000>` (Python:
`context_noise=...`, SkyReels `addnoise_condition` precedent, ~20) optionally perturbs the
head in latent space, deterministic per seed. Both are recorded in metadata
(`context_image_paths`, `context_noise`), replayed by `--config-from-metadata`, and advertised
as the additive `supports_context_frames` field on the `wan.first-frame` capability row
(introduced in capabilities schema 6; current payload schema 11). EXPERIMENTAL zero-shot behavior with a measured probe
(backlog 0102): the K=5 head carried seam motion speed (magnitude ratio 0.90 vs the
single-frame baseline's 1.90 double-speed restart) at the cost of a mild ~2-frame
flare/exposure step at the conditioned-to-free boundary; hosts assembling films should trim
the predecessor at the FIRST handover frame (the head is regenerated, not copied).

`--svi-anchor-image` (Python: `generate_video(svi_anchor_image_path=...)`) enables SVI 2.0 Pro
chain conditioning on the same Wan A14B i2v route (EXPERIMENTAL, backlog 0103): every clip
conditions on `[anchor_latent, motion_latent?, zero-latents]` — one persistent anchor image
re-injected into every clip of a chain (identity), the previous clip's final denoised latent
handed over via the exported `<output>.svi_latent.safetensors` and `--svi-motion-latent`
(momentum; count via `--svi-motion-latent-count`, default 1), and TRUE zero-latent padding
(not the stock zero-frame VAE encode). Requires the SVI error-recycling LoRA pair
(`--svi-lora-high`/`--svi-lora-low`, fixed scale 1.0, strict key-match: any unmatched key
aborts; the pack is likewise rejected on non-SVI runs). Conflicts with `--image-path`,
`--last-image`, `--context-frames`, `--video-path`; TI2V-5B and VACE reject before weight
load; continuations >65 frames warn. Metadata records `svi_*` truth including
`svi_assembly_trim_frames` (drop that many leading frames of each continuation at assembly:
`1 + 4 x count`); hosts gate on the additive `supports_svi` capability field (capabilities
schema 7; current payload schema 11). Use a unique seed per clip; author-documented Lightning coexistence sets
lightx2v HIGH scale 0.5-0.6, LOW 1.0.

`--denoising-step-list 1000 750 500 250` (Python: `denoising_step_list=[...]`) runs an exact
denoising timestep grid (strictly decreasing integers in `[1, 1000]`) instead of a
count-derived schedule — the LightX2V distill contract — on both `unipc` and `euler` solvers.
The transformer sees exactly the requested timesteps; sigma follows `t / 1000`. Grid entries
are final, already-shifted timesteps, so the flag is mutually exclusive with `--steps` and
`--flow-shift`, and rejected for video-to-video (strength truncation would drop grid points)
and on Wan VACE. Metadata records `denoising_step_list` with `steps` set to the grid length and
`flow_shift` recorded as null, and `--config-from-metadata` replays it.

Wan uses the model's official default negative prompt when `--negative-prompt` is omitted. Pass
`--negative ""` or `--negative-prompt ""` to intentionally run without a negative prompt for simple
abstract scenes where the default negative prompt creates unwanted texture. Wan prompts have a
hard UMT5 budget of `--max-sequence-length` tokens (default `512`); text beyond it never
conditions the video. Runs that exceed the budget print one stderr warning naming the counts
("prompt truncated: 547 -> 512 UMT5 tokens") and record `prompt_tokens` / `prompt_truncated`
(plus the negative-prompt pair when guidance actually encodes the negative) in the metadata
sidecar.

Prompt-guided video-to-video is public on `Wan2.2-T2V-A14B` only: one source video via
`--video-path`, one prompt, optional `--video-strength` (default `0.8`, range `(0, 1]`), and
`--solver unipc` required. Camera path, framing, and scene layout survive at typical strengths;
subject gestures and timing are re-synthesized, not copied. Measured ladder (docs/wan-video.md,
"Motion Fidelity Versus Strength"): gestures survive at strength 0.5-0.6 with 20 steps CFG-on
(gesture-timing r 0.86-0.90), mostly at 0.7 (r 0.73), and are re-synthesized at the 0.8 default
(r 0.20) and the 4-step Lightning point (sigma 0.94); the Lightning fast path cannot reach the
motion-preserving band. Use `--video-mask-path` to preserve regions exactly, including their
motion. All image and video metadata (sidecar and embedded) carries `metadata_schema_version`
(currently 2, additive-only evolution; v2 renamed the masked-edit key
`masked_warm_start_strength` to `mask_strength` and replay reads both spellings). The run denoises `floor(steps x video_strength)` effective steps; saved
metadata records the requested `steps` plus `effective_steps`, `video_strength`,
`high_noise_stage_skipped`, `source_video_audio_present`, `source_video_resampled`, and
source-clip frame count, duration, and fps. The source is resampled onto the `--fps` timeline at
decode, so the output keeps real-time speed regardless of source fps (matching fps passes frames
through untouched; upsampling above the source fps duplicates frames with a warning). Source
audio is copied onto the saved output best-effort, trimmed to the output duration; on failure the
video is saved silent with a printed reason plus manual remux command, and metadata records
`audio_copied` / `audio_copy_reason`. Below roughly strength
`0.7` the A14B high-noise stage is skipped and `--guidance` is inactive (a warning is printed).
Source frames are stretched to the requested canvas by default, so the requested aspect ratio
should match the source; `--canvas-policy source-aspect` derives the canvas from the clip instead,
and `--resize-mode crop|pad` maps the frames (and any mask, through the same geometry) without
distortion. Plain video-to-video and VACE print a warning when ratios differ by more than 2% under
the stretching `resize` mode. Masked video-to-video adds one static image mask via `--video-mask-path`: white marks the
region the model may change, black regions are locked to the source video at every denoising step
and match it up to VAE round-trip precision; masks are binarized at 50% on the latent grid,
all-black masks fail before model load, and the mask path is recorded in metadata and replayed by
`--config-from-metadata`. The A14B route rejects reference images and VACE-style controls -
those live on the natively ported `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B-diffusers` (`wan-vace`) model:
`--reference-image` (repeatable) injects a pictured object into a new scene with or without a
source video (segment the subject onto a plain white background - crops that keep background
weaken identity transfer and full-scene references lose the subject), `--video-mask-path`
feeds learned VACE mask conditioning with `--vace-masked-region` selecting the semantics
(`generate`, the default, gray-fills the editable region per the official VACE inpainting
convention so the model synthesizes new structure; `repaint` keeps the source content and
restyles in place), `--conditioning-scale` (default 1.0) controls the branch strength,
`--video-strength`/`guidance_2` are rejected, and the port is verified stage-by-stage against
the diffusers reference (proof in docs/assets/validation/wan-vace-2026-07-06/). TI2V-5B
and I2V-A14B reject `--video-path`. The exact reproducible proof command and included artifacts
live in `docs/wan-video.md` and `docs/assets/examples/spaceship-v2v/`.

---

## MiniMax-H3 Video With Audio

MiniMax-H3 (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`) generates a 24 fps clip and a synchronized stereo soundtrack
from one structured prompt; MLX-Gen saves both in a single MP4 with an AAC track (32 kHz). Three
catalog entries share the weights: `minimax-h3` (base, 50 steps, shifts 12/3, `1344x768`),
`minimax-h3-turbo` (lightx2v 8-step Turbo adapter trained at 768p, shifts 6/3, `1344x768`), and
`minimax-h3-turbo-544p` (8-step adapter trained at 544p on mixed aspect ratios, shifts 12/3,
`960x544`). `--steps` counts transformer evaluations. The Turbo entries attach their adapter
automatically and `mlxgen download --model minimax-h3-turbo-544p` fetches it with the snapshot.

Adapters: `--lora-paths` replaces the automatic Turbo adapter, so a style or character adapter on a
Turbo entry is passed together with the Turbo file (`hf:lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo/<file>` plus the
adapter, one `--lora-scales` value each). Two key layouts load: PEFT files over the diffusers module
names (the lightx2v files) and community files trained against the original checkpoint's names
(civitai, ai-toolkit, ComfyUI, kohya, musubi-tuner: fused `attn.qkv_proj`, `mlp.fc1`, `blocks.N`,
with or without a `diffusion_model.` prefix, PEFT or kohya naming, flattened `lora_unet_` keys). The
fused QKV shares one `lora_A` and splits `lora_B` into `to_q`/`to_k`/`to_v` row thirds and `fc1`'s
`[gate; value]` halves swap onto the SwiGLU's `[value; gate]`, as the diffusers converter does. Scale
follows the file: metadata `alpha / rank`, kohya `.alpha` per module, `alpha == rank` for a PEFT file
with neither. DiffSynth-Studio exports (per-head interleaved fused QKV) are refused with a reason.
Metadata exports list each adapter with its scale and matched / unmatched key counts
(`lora_application_reports`). Included evidence: the civitai Skeletor adapter (ai-toolkit, rank 8)
stacked on the 544p Turbo adapter at `640x352`, same seed with and without, plus a second seed.
Steps: the 544p 8-step adapter is recommended at 8 or 4 evaluations by lightx2v, the 768p 8-step
adapter at 8, the dedicated 4-step adapters at 4 (with `--video-shift 6`); 8 is the setting of every
included clip, 4 the draft setting. Measured on one seed at `640x352`: the 544p 8-step adapter at 4
steps keeps its 8-step staging in a third of the time, the 4-step v1.2 adapter renders a brighter
take and gains little from 8 steps; the soundtrack keeps its own schedule at any step count.

Prompt format: `--prompt` fills `integrated_multimodal_description`, `--soundscape` fills
`overall_soundscape`, `--music` fills `non_diegetic_music`; a prompt that already carries the
section labels is passed through verbatim. There is no negative prompt and no guidance scale. The
three kinds of sound have three places: ambient and diegetic sound in the soundscape, score in the
music section, and speech written into the description with a stable speaker id and dialogue tags
(`The woman ... (S1) says: <d>[English] ...</d>`; `says in an off-screen voiceover` for narration).
The model generates the voice and animates the speaker's mouth; 11 dialogue languages are listed as
stably supported, and `<d>`, `</d>`, `<|cutoff|>` and the lyric/caption markers are dedicated
vocabulary tokens that MLX-Gen tokenizes exactly as the reference does.
Frames round up to `17n + 5` (fourteen counts, 124 to 345, 5.17 to 14.375 s) and warn when they do; width and height are multiples of 32 within
1:4 to 4:1. `--no-audio` writes a silent clip. Metadata records `steps` (transformer evaluations),
`video_shift`, `audio_shift`, `num_inference_steps` (the scheduler grid, one more than `steps`),
`text_tokens`, `duration_seconds`, and `audio_present`, `audio_source`,
`audio_channels`, `audio_sample_rate`, `audio_duration_seconds`, `audio_muxed`, `audio_codec`,
`audio_mux_mode` (a sidecar `<output>.wav` and `audio_sidecar_path` when muxing fails).

Requirements and cost: about 140 GB of disk for the snapshot plus 1.4 GB per adapter; run with
`--quantize 8` (shard-by-shard load-time quantization) on a 128 GB Mac, or prepare a local 75 GB
mixed q8/BF16 package once with `mlxgen prepare --model minimax-h3 --quantize 8 --path
models/minimax-h3-8bit` and load it with `--model <path>` plus `--base-model minimax-h3-turbo-544p`
(or `minimax-h3-turbo`) for a Turbo schedule; prepared packages stream shard by shard too. The MLX
free-buffer cache follows the process default (up to 8 GiB), adjustable with `--mlx-cache-limit-gb`.
Measured on an Apple M5 Max with 124 frames: `960x544` Turbo 8 steps at ~55 s per step (about 8
minutes of denoise and decode, 80 GB MLX peak, 88 GB process footprint); `1344x768` Turbo 8 steps at
about 5 minutes per step (93 GB footprint). The first load reads 133 GB of shards (a few minutes); later loads from the page cache take
seconds.

Driving it from an application: `mlxgen capabilities` publishes everything needed to build controls
without hardcoding the model — `generates_audio`, `audio_channels`, `audio_sample_rate`, the
`prompt_sections` descriptors (each with the engine's literal label and the option that fills it),
the frame grid (`min_frames` 124, `max_frames` 345, `frame_multiple` 17, `frame_remainder` 5,
`frame_rounding` up), `output_fps` 24, and the per-entry `default_steps` / `default_width` /
`default_height` / `default_flow_shift` / `default_audio_shift`. Each entry publishes its own label.
The shift field is named for the concept, not for one family's spelling: Wan calls the same control
`--flow-shift` and MiniMax-H3 calls it `--video-shift`, and both publish `supports_flow_shift: true`.
Each row also carries `flow_shift_option` and `flow_shift_parameter`, the CLI flag and Python keyword
that route uses, so a host emits the right one without a per-family table; both are null exactly when
`supports_flow_shift` is false. `--low-ram` works here as on every other generate route, and the
payload's `universal_options` names the options every generate route in this build accepts, so an
application reads the build instead of gating on the release number.
It also publishes the precision and memory contract in bytes: `weight_precision` bf16,
`unquantized_weights_bytes` (125 GiB, which is 97% of a 128 GiB Mac, so `--quantize 8` is required
rather than optional there and the runtime refuses an impossible load with an explanatory error),
`recommended_quantize` 8, `validated_quantization_bits` [8], and `measured_runs`: measured runs with
their outcome, the highest process footprint observed, and the conditions that make each reproducible.
Peak memory follows the packed sequence length rather than the canvas and frame count separately, and
`peak_bytes_fixed` / `peak_bytes_per_packed_row` publish the measured line through it;
`max_validated_frames` says how far the evidence goes, where `max_frames` is the decode grid. Runs
that the OS killed are published too, and before a long run the runtime estimates the peak, refuses
what cannot fit and warns when a request is close enough that other resident processes decide it.
`supports_guidance` is published separately from `supports_negative_prompt`, since the two diverge in
both directions across the catalog.
Progress phases are `start`, `denoise`, `decode`, `generated`, then the CLI's `save` and `complete`,
delivered to both a `progress_callback` and the model's registry.

Python: `MiniMaxH3(model_config=ModelConfig.minimax_h3_turbo_544p(), quantize=8)` and
`generate_video(seed, prompt, soundscape=..., music=..., width=..., height=..., num_frames=...,
num_inference_steps=..., video_shift=..., audio_shift=..., generate_audio=True,
progress_callback=...)`; the result's `audio` is a `GeneratedAudio` (`waveform` `(2, samples)`
float32, `sample_rate` 32000). `--image-path` selects first-frame image-to-video: the canvas follows the keyframe's aspect ratio at the
entry's short edge unless `width`/`height` are given, the keyframe is stretched onto it and conditions
both the latent rows and the text sequence through the Qwen3-VL vision tower. Motion prompts for a
keyframe work best as one continuous action with its end state ("lifts straight up in one smooth
motion and leaves through the top of the frame"), naming what must stay unchanged, with a continuous
soundscape and explicit exclusions; the starship and takeoff sheets in `docs/assets/minimax-h3/`
carry the complete prompts. Limits: reference-to-video and the closing keyframe are not available
yet; no published package (prepare one locally); the 768p canvas is slow on Apple Silicon. MiniMax-H3 is released under the MiniMax H3 Community License, which restricts use
in some territories; read it on the model card before downloading or distributing weights or
outputs. Every component was verified against the diffusers 0.40 reference (layouts and schedules
bit-exact, transformer / conditioner / VAEs at fp32 rounding noise on real weights).

## Bernini-R 1.3B

MLX-Gen exposes ByteDance's Bernini-R 1.3B renderer through a dedicated Wan-family runtime. The
surface is experimental and not yet promoted, but seven official public 1.3B example rows plus
`ads2v` at mid profile are qualitatively accepted with committed proof. Use it for development and
diagnosis when ordinary images should act as semantic references rather than first frames, or when
a source video should be edited with those references:

- one to eight ordered `--reference-image` inputs and no video select reference-to-video (R2V);
- one `--video` plus one to eight references select reference-guided video editing (RV2V);
- one `--video` with no references selects source-only prompt-guided video editing (V2V).

The parity harness also replays upstream `t2i`, `i2i`, `t2v`, `mv2v`, and `ads2v` task types.
The planner-backed Bernini motion-rewrite workflow, LoRA, masks, warm-start strength,
first/last frame anchors, multi-frame continuation, and multiple source videos are not supported by
this renderer-only integration.

Committed proof with **full upstream prompts and contact sheets** per row:
`docs/assets/validation/bernini-r-1.3b-2026-08-11/README.md`. Row status:
`docs/assets/validation/bernini-r-1.3b-2026-08-04/official_example_parity_matrix.md`.

Accepted rows: `t2i`, `i2i`, `t2v`, `r2v`, `rv2v_case1`, `v2v_case1`, `mv2v` (three caveats),
`ads2v` at mid profile. `r2v_case2` and `v2v_case3` need tuned settings for their best results;
the recipes and worked examples are documented in `docs/bernini.md` (Task-Specific Recipes) and
the parity bundle (`r2v_case2_tuned`, `v2v_case3_mv2vprefix`).

Download the recommended BF16 package (runtime dtypes, 42% smaller, bit-identical output):

```sh
mlxgen download --model bernini-r-1.3b-bf16
```

This alias selects the pinned `AbstractFramework/bernini-r-1.3B-diffusers-bf16` revision
(approximately 15.6 GiB cold). The FP32 source package remains available via
`mlxgen download --model bernini-r-1.3b`, selecting the pinned
`ByteDance/Bernini-R-1.3B-Diffusers` revision (approximately 27 GiB cold). The main
`ByteDance/Bernini-R` A14B repository and similarly named third-party repositories fail closed;
they are never silently rewritten to the 1.3B renderer. Both packages preflight with 2 GiB of
free-space headroom and execute identically at run time: text encoder and transformer in BF16
(with small FP32 keep-sets) and the VAE in FP32. Quantized variants are not supported:
`--quantize` values are rejected for this model.

Example R2V request (diagnostic bounded profile; see the parity bundle for official full prompts):

```sh
mlxgen generate \
  --model bernini-r-1.3b \
  --reference-image subject.png \
  --reference-image garment.png \
  --prompt "Place the subject from image0 in a studio, wearing the garment from image1, slowly turning toward the camera" \
  --width 320 --height 192 --frames 17 --fps 16 \
  --steps 20 --max-condition-size 256 \
  --seed 42 --low-ram --metadata \
  --output referenced.mp4
```

Official quality defaults are 848x480, 81 frames, 16 fps, 40 steps, UniPC, and flow shift 5. The
maximum condition side defaults to 848; its accepted range is 16-1280 in multiples of 16.
Source-video modes preserve the source aspect ratio with resize-only conditioning: the source
video's long edge is capped at the condition limit (never upscaled, snapped to multiples of 16)
and that resolved size is the output canvas. Their `--frames` value is a maximum because source
duration/fps may clamp the actual `4n+1` output; metadata `output_frames` is authoritative.
Prompts have a hard 512-token UMT5 budget. R2V uses text guidance 4.0 and reference guidance 4.5
with APG; RV2V adds source guidance 1.25 and uses chained CFG; V2V uses text guidance 4.0 with
APG. Tuned recipes for many-reference binding (`--reference-guidance 6.0`, seed variation) and
structure-changing edits (Python API `task_type="mv2v"`, guidance 5.0) are documented in
`docs/bernini.md`.

The bounded low-RAM matrix peaks at 9.45 GB whole-process physical footprint on the 128 GB
validation host, so the tested shapes fit an 18 GB-class envelope; this is not a direct 18 GB-host
proof. The earlier schema-v3 bundle used a bounded 17-frame profile and is superseded by the
full-profile parity bundle; it stays discoverable through the framework registry:

```sh
mlxgen validation --model bernini-r-1.3b
```

See `docs/bernini.md` for the full CLI/Python contract, guidance table, capacity limits, official
example catalog, and proof links.

---

## Generation Previews

A preview is a full-resolution image of a generation in progress, decoded from the latent at a
given denoising step. `--stepwise-image-output-dir` writes one PNG per step, and
`--preview-decoder auto|tiny|full` selects the decoder: `auto` (default) uses the published tiny
autoencoder for the model's latent space when it is available and downloaded, and otherwise
previews through the full VAE. Tiny decoders are mapped explicitly per latent space and never by
latent-channel count: `madebyollin/taef1` serves the FLUX.1 latent space (flux, Z-Image) and
`madebyollin/taef2` serves the FLUX.2 latent space (FLUX.2 Klein, ERNIE-Image, Bonsai). Other
families preview through the full VAE. Download a decoder once with
`mlxgen download --model madebyollin/taef1`.

Final outputs are always decoded with the full VAE, so a run with previews enabled produces a
byte-identical image to the same run without them. Measured on M5 Max at `512x512` with FLUX.2
Klein 4B q8: a full VAE frame decode takes 203 ms versus 19 ms for the tiny decoder, so
previewing every step costs roughly 8% extra wall time instead of roughly 86%. Choosing a decoder
does not meaningfully change single-image generation time, because both paths share the denoising
loop. Preview fidelity against the full VAE decode of the same latent reaches 34.8 dB PSNR
(SSIM 0.975) at the final step on Z-Image Turbo; differences concentrate in fine texture, so
previews suit composition and direction judgments rather than final-quality decisions.

Applications render live previews by registering an in-loop callback, decoding the step's latents
with `PreviewDecoder.resolve(model, mode="auto")` (which returns `None` when no tiny decoder
exists, so keep a `model.vae.decode` fallback), and converting with `ImageUtil.to_pil_image`.
Image tiny decoders reject multi-frame latents rather than previewing only the first frame.

## Repeat-Run And Application Performance

Options that matter when Wan runs repeatedly in one process or inside an application:

- Prompt-embed disk cache (default on): identical prompt encodes are served from a small on-disk
  safetensors cache (LRU-bounded) instead of reloading the ~11 GB UMT5 text encoder; a cache hit
  does not import torch. Opt out with `--no-prompt-cache` (CLI) or
  `prompt_embed_disk_cache=False` (constructor).
- Resident text encoder: `--keep-text-encoder` / `keep_text_encoder_resident=True` keeps the UMT5
  encoder loaded between generations in one process, for hosts that chain new-prompt scene
  generations. The default releases it after encoding.
- `--no-validate-health` (Wan video generation and SeedVR2 video restore): skips the post-save
  full-file health re-decode for applications that probe the saved file themselves. Recorded as
  `health_check: "skipped"` in metadata and the `save` runtime event.
- `--compile-transformer` (opt-in): runs each Wan denoiser as a compiled MLX graph for roughly
  2-6% per-step gain; output is close to but not bit-identical with eager mode, so it never
  becomes a default.
- A14B inactive-expert release (automatic on disk-prequantized dual-expert runs): the ~14 GB
  high-noise expert is released after its per-item denoise phase and rebuilt when the next item
  needs it; override with `--release-inactive-denoiser` / `--no-release-inactive-denoiser`.
- `--json-events`: the `start` event carries resolved output `width`/`height`; the `save` event
  carries `fps`, `width`, `height`, `total_frames`, and `health_check`, so applications can build
  artifact records without probe decodes.
- Python embedding: `load_generation_model(..., model_kwargs={...})` forwards constructor extras
  (such as the two encoder options above), and video `save_kwargs` accept `validate_health=False`
  plus `export_json_metadata=True`. See `docs/python-integration.md`.

FLUX.2 resident instances reuse work across calls automatically: identical prompts on the same
instance are served from a bounded 8-entry prompt-embed LRU (skipping the ~1 s Qwen3 re-encode
across txt2img, edit, inpaint, and outpaint), and the compiled denoise predict is cached per
instance and reused across same-structure calls (invalidated on transformer replacement, LoRA
application, training preview, LoRA bake, and low-RAM transformer release). No flags are
involved; both caches are per-instance and process-local.

---

## Runtime Memory And Load Defaults

MLX-Gen applies two machine-derived runtime-memory behaviors by default on every model family.
Both are visible, bounded, and overridable:

- MLX buffer-cache limit: when no limit is set, the first model load in a process applies
  `total RAM / 8`, clamped to `[1 GiB, 8 GiB]`, exactly once, announced with one stderr line.
  Low-RAM mode keeps its 1 GB default. A pre-existing limit at or below half of physical RAM
  (set by a host through `mx.set_cache_limit`) is treated as deliberate, preserved, and
  announced instead of overridden. Override with `--mlx-cache-limit-gb <gb>` on CLIs or
  `MFLUX_MLX_CACHE_LIMIT_GB=<gb>` for Python-API hosts; pass `-1` for explicitly unlimited.
  Precedence: CLI flag > env var > low-RAM default > machine ladder. The limit bounds only the
  FREE cache; resident weights and in-flight activations are unaffected.
- Weight prefetch at load: weight files loaded from HF-repo layouts are sequentially read into
  the OS page cache before use, so page-cold weights fault in at sequential SSD speed instead
  of random-access speed. Prepared MLX-Gen packages are not prefetched — they are written in
  module-tree order and materialize near-sequentially on their own. Already-resident files are
  detected (`mincore`) and skipped, and the prefetch is skipped entirely when the selected
  files exceed half of physical RAM. Set `MFLUX_NO_WEIGHT_PREFETCH=1` to disable it.

There is no published TI2V-5B q4/mixed q4/q8 package yet.

MLX-Gen model packages use the MLX-Gen/mflux saved-weight layout. They are intended for MLX-Gen and
compatible mflux code, not direct Diffusers or Transformers `from_pretrained()` loading.

## Quantization Summary

MLX-Gen treats low-bit model preparation as model-specific. Qwen and ERNIE use mixed q4/q8 policies
because fully q4 layouts can visibly degrade generation. Bonsai uses Prism's pre-packed ternary
2-bit checkpoint rather than MLX-Gen `prepare`.

Wan A14B uses a mixed q8/BF16 policy for 8-bit packages:

- q8 storage for bulky transformer block linears;
- BF16 for the Wan VAE;
- BF16 for sensitive conditioning/output projection paths;
- BF16 for the UMT5 text encoder, tokenizer files, scheduler metadata, norms, convolutions, and
  non-quantizable parameters.

Important correction (2026-07-05): since the 2026-06-12 runtime-precision fix, Wan q8 packages
(A14B and TI2V-5B) dequantize all transformer-block linears to BF16 at load to protect output
quality. Wan q8 is therefore a storage/download saving only; runtime memory matches the BF16
package. The historical benchmark numbers below predate that fix. Re-measured on 2026-07-05 at the
same T2V-A14B profile, the q8 package peaks at 27.8 GiB MLX versus 27.7 GiB for BF16. Plan Wan
memory as if running BF16.

For TI2V-5B, the upstream source snapshot is about 31.9 GiB and stores transformer and VAE files as
FP32 while the UMT5 text encoder is BF16. MLX-Gen loads and converts Wan transformer/VAE weights at
BF16 runtime precision. The published BF16 package is about 21.2 GiB and the q8 package is
about 16.9 GiB; BF16 is mainly a smaller source-equivalent package, not a separate runtime-memory
optimization. A TI2V-5B 1280x704, 17-frame, 20-step benchmark with
`--negative-prompt ""` produced byte-identical decoded frames for source and the BF16 package, and a
matching q8/BF16 output with mean frame MAE 1.66 versus source/BF16. The MP4s, contact sheet, and
metrics are linked from `docs/quantization.md`. The measured TI2V profile was:

- TI2V-5B upstream source: 31.9 GiB storage, 10.6 GiB Wan MLX model footprint, 10.3 GiB MLX
  active after generation, 102.7 GiB physical peak, 13.7 GiB max RSS, 58.5 GiB MLX peak,
  216.2 s.
- TI2V-5B BF16 package: 21.2 GiB storage, 10.6 GiB Wan MLX model footprint, 10.3 GiB MLX active
  after generation, 102.6 GiB physical peak, 14.5 GiB max RSS, 58.5 GiB MLX peak, 261.6 s.
- TI2V-5B mixed q8/BF16: 16.9 GiB storage, 6.3 GiB Wan MLX model footprint, 6.1 GiB MLX active
  after generation, 103.7 GiB physical peak, 13.8 GiB max RSS, 54.2 GiB MLX peak, 243.4 s.

The TI2V-5B rows above were measured before the 2026-06-12 runtime-precision change and describe
storage and loaded/active model bytes only. Wan q8 packages dequantize every transformer-block
linear to BF16 at load, so runtime memory matches the BF16 rows and q8 is a storage and download
saving. See `docs/quantization.md` for the re-measured figures.

On an Apple M5 Max with 128 GB unified memory, A14B measurements use short low-RAM profiles:

- T2V-A14B BF16: 64.1 GiB disk, 33.0 GiB physical peak, 31.8 GiB max RSS, 27.7 GiB MLX peak,
  152.7 s on 384x224, 33 frames, 12 steps, 8 fps.
- T2V-A14B mixed q8/BF16: 39.5 GiB disk, 20.7 GiB physical peak, 19.5 GiB max RSS, 15.5 GiB MLX
  peak, 154.8 s on the same profile.
- I2V-A14B BF16: 64.1 GiB disk, 33.7 GiB physical peak, 31.8 GiB max RSS, 28.2 GiB MLX peak,
  228.2 s on 384x384, 33 frames, 12 steps, 8 fps.
- I2V-A14B mixed q8/BF16: 39.5 GiB disk, 21.5 GiB physical peak, 19.6 GiB max RSS, 15.9 GiB MLX
  peak, 242.2 s on the same profile.

In those benchmark runs, mixed q8/BF16 reduced disk usage by about 38% versus BF16 MLX-Gen
packages. It is a storage and download saving, not a runtime-memory or speed improvement. Full-size
Wan video memory and runtime vary with resolution, frame count, step count, task, cache settings,
and prompt/image conditioning.

The 0.18.11 release validates the published A14B q8 handles on a short practical profile. The T2V
handle generated 480x240, 41 frames, 15 steps in 348.9 s with 19.5 GiB max RSS. The I2V handle used
a 480x240 target, preserved the source aspect ratio as 448x256, generated 41 frames at 15 steps in
360.3 s with 19.6 GiB max RSS. The MP4s, metadata JSON, and contact sheets are linked from
`docs/quantization.md`.

---

## Ecosystem

MLX-Gen is used by:

- AbstractVision: the direct integration layer for abstracting generative image and video
  capabilities across local and hosted providers (https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractvision);
- AbstractCore: the endpoint layer that can expose OpenAI-compatible image/video capabilities backed
  by AbstractVision providers (https://abstractcore.ai/);
- AbstractFlow: a visual workflow authoring layer that can compose generative image/video nodes with
  other media, text, and agent workflows (https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractflow).

MLX-Gen owns the local MLX runtime boundary: model loading, capability resolution, quantized local
formats, fail-fast missing-artifact behavior, and progress events.

---

## Safety And Contribution Notes

Model weights remain governed by their source licenses and access requirements. Hugging Face tokens
and private paths should not be committed. Security issues should be reported according to
`SECURITY.md`.

Contributors should keep user-facing docs aligned with runnable commands, avoid documenting
unsupported routes, and follow the model-backed validation policy in the ADRs when adding new model
support.
